description:
FILED s524 (Fable, 2026-10-22) from the round-4 companion on MAIN-READY-43 and four one-file runs: op/each.t is 48/16 on every run, but the blessed failing row `Check length of "\x{10fffd}"` (perl-suite-fails.tsv) came back as `Check length of "\x{123}"` (wt-s523b, and one of two consecutive runs on wt-s523d) and as `Check length of "\022"` (the round-4 run) -- a 1 NEW / 1 FIXED pair with unchanged counts.  PRE-EXISTING (the snapshot row dates from s514e).

The test (t/op/each.t:153-161): my %u = ("\x{12}" => f, "\x{123}" => fo, "\x{1234}" => foo); $u{"\x{12345}"} = bar;  = zap; foreach (keys %u) { is(length(), 1, "Check length of " . _qq $_); $u2{$_} = $u{$_} }.  A standalone probe of exactly that hash + loop prints len=1 for all five keys on perl, the 2534d7d0 base and the -43 tree (scratchpad each-len.pl) -- so length() is right; ONE iteration of the loop inside the test file fails, and which one depends on the iteration order.

DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (3 minutes, not yet taken): (1) does PCL evaluate `is()`'s arguments left to right?  `_qq $_` calls t/test.pl's display(), which may write $_ (a s/// over an alias) -- if PCL evaluates the description argument BEFORE `length()`, the first or last iterated key reads a clobbered $_; probe `sub f { $_ = "xx"; 1 } for ("a") { print length(), f(), "\n" }` perl vs PCL.  (2) print $_ (as hex) and length() per iteration INSIDE a copy of each.t's loop with t/test.pl loaded (tools/pclperl-for-tests), to see which iteration fails and what $_ holds then.  (3) the iteration ORDER itself: perl-tests/each.t runs under the sweep with a stable order? -- PCL's `keys` order for these five keys differs between runs (sxhash of a string should be deterministic; something else varies -- check whether the hash is keyed by eq on fresh strings / by address).

RECORD: the companion snapshot row for op/each.t carries the flap note (baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv, s524); the blessed row stays `\x{10fffd}` until the cause is found -- a 1 NEW / 1 FIXED pair on op/each.t at 48/16 is this flap, not a mover.
subject: UNSTABLE ROW (companion op/each.t): one of the five `Check length of ...` rows fails and WHICH key fails flaps run to run on the same tree (hash order) -- the standalone five-key shape prints every length = 1, so the failure is in the row's context, not in length()
